messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.

You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.

Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.

- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Genesis 19:24: "Then Yahweh rained on Sodom and on Gomorrah sulfur and fire from Yahweh out of the sky."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs
People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers.
Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals.
Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.
Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Sodom: a walled city of sun-dried mud-brick on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, its gate the centre of civic life; flat-roofed houses stacked close, date palms and irrigated gardens beyond the walls, and low hills to the east; the Valley of Siddim nearby, its ground dark with tar pits.
- Gomorrah: a walled mud-brick town on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, flat green pasture and irrigated fields around it, date palms and tamarisk along the ditches, tar pits in the low valley of Siddim to the east, distant hills rising beyond the plain.
- Only Sodom, Gomorrah have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Burning cities of Sodom and Gomorrah under a rain of fire and sulfur from the sky
Action: Blazing sulfur and fire pour down from a dark cloud onto the walled towns
Setting: Well-watered plain of the Jordan with irrigated green gardens, mud-brick towns and palm groves
Secondary elements: Dark smoke rising from the burning cities, scattered fleeing shapes in the distance, dim outline of Zoar
Mood: Awe, dread and solemn grief, restrained rather than spectacular
Time of day: Dawn breaking into day, still dry air, smoke and fire glowing over the plain
Composition: Wide view from a rise above the plain, cities below the fiery cloud, horizon with sunrise

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: The sun had risen on the earth when Lot came to Zoar.
- After: He overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew on the ground.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

content.text:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Israelite people (the children of Israel); Moses

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- Only The Israelite people (the children of Israel), Moses, Red Sea have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Israelite families walking in a column across the sea floor, Moses near the front with his staff.
Action: The people step forward steadily over the dry seabed while the water stands in towering walls on either side.
Setting: The middle of the sea basin with wet sand underfoot and high water walls on both sides.
Secondary elements: Pillar of cloud and fire glowing above the camp, spray hanging over the water walls, children and goods carried by the crowd.
Mood: Awe, cautious hope and quiet urgency.
Time of day: Night turning toward dawn, heavy cloud and a cool east wind.
Composition: Wide view from low on the seabed looking along the column toward the far shore, water walls framing both sides.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):

- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, the camp of Israel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses standing forward with one hand raised toward the gathered people, Aaron beside him in plain linen priestly garments.
Action: Moses speaks the distinction of clean and unclean animals, pointing toward the hills where a pig roots in dry ground.
Setting: The wilderness camp of Israel with woven tents around the central tabernacle and dry desert hills beyond.
Secondary elements: Clusters of Israelite men, women and children in woven tunics and cloaks, a few goats and sheep grazing at the edge of the camp, a faint radiance and cloud glow above the tabernacle.
Mood: Attentive, solemn and orderly, with a sense of holy instruction.
Time of day: Midday under clear dry sky, bright sun and a faint warm wind over the sand.
Composition: Wide view from slightly below the crowd, with Moses and Aaron central in the foreground and the tabernacle rising in the middle distance.

Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- Before: The hare, because it chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, is unclean to you.

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Judges 19:29: "When he had come into his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Levite husband of the concubine; The Levite's concubine

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.
- The Levite's concubine: a young woman in her late teens, slender, of modest height, olive-brown skin, dark hair bound back and covered with a linen veil. Plain woven tunic of undyed wool with a dull red border and a long cloak of rust-brown wool. Simple features, dignified and quiet, with a gentle face. No jewellery beyond a bronze ring.
- Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.
- Only The Levite husband of the concubine, The Levite's concubine, Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: The Levite standing in the dim house, knife held low at his side, over the still form of his concubine laid on the floor.
Action: The moment before the cutting begins; the knife is lowered, not raised, and the body is stillness.
Setting: Interior of a modest stone house in Gibeah, with a low wooden bench, woven mats and a clay lamp.
Secondary elements: Lamplight on the knife blade and bare floor; a folded cloak and the donkey visible faintly through the open doorway.
Mood: Grim, solemn and horrified, with heavy grief and restraint rather than spectacle.
Time of day: Deep night in the house, still cool air, with grey pre-dawn light beginning at the doorway.
Composition: Eye-level view from the doorway, the Levite in the middle ground facing inward, the body low in the foreground, lamp at one side for light.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Job

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.
- The whirlwind: a great column of storm wind rising from a dark wilderness sky, funnelling dust, torn cloud and scattered grit in dense swirling bands. Heavy grey-brown cloud churns above, its edges lit faintly from behind. Low scrub and bare desert ground are flattened and whipped by the gale.
- The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.
- Only Job, The whirlwind, The ash heap have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Job, seated and upright on the ash heap, gazing upward into the storm.
Action: Job lifts his head and braces himself as the voice speaks from within the whirlwind.
Setting: Barren ash heap outside a village, bare ground, broken pottery, distant hills.
Secondary elements: A violent whirlwind of dust and ash swirls across the ground, with radiant cloud and fire-tinged light gathering within it.
Mood: Awe, grief and tense expectancy, reverent and grounded.
Time of day: Late afternoon turning toward dusk, low fading sunlight breaking through storm clouds.
Composition: Job in the lower foreground on the ash heap, the whirlwind rising behind and above him across the open ground, distant hills at the horizon.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Job

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.
- The whirlwind: a great column of storm wind rising from a dark wilderness sky, funnelling dust, torn cloud and scattered grit in dense swirling bands. Heavy grey-brown cloud churns above, its edges lit faintly from behind. Low scrub and bare desert ground are flattened and whipped by the gale.
- The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.
- Only Job, The whirlwind, The ash heap have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Job, seated and upright on the ash heap, gazing upward into the storm.
Action: Job lifts his head and braces himself as the voice speaks from within the whirlwind.
Setting: Barren ash heap outside a village, bare ground, broken pottery, distant hills.
Secondary elements: A violent whirlwind of dust and ash swirls across the ground, with radiant cloud and fire-tinged light gathering within it.
Mood: Awe, grief and tense expectancy, reverent and grounded.
Time of day: Late afternoon turning toward dusk, low fading sunlight breaking through storm clouds.
Composition: Job in the lower foreground on the ash heap, the whirlwind rising behind and above him across the open ground, distant hills at the horizon.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.

The scene should show: The Shulammite. Its description: The Shulammite standing upright among blooming flowers, head slightly lifted; Wild roses and lilies in the grass, distant vineyards and stone village houses, a shepherd's staff resting nearby
First describe the edges, the bright areas and any marks, then answer.
- figure_in_light: true if a head, face, hands, shoulders or a robed or human-shaped body appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. A faint or translucent figure counts if you can point to its head, face, hands or body outline. A flame, a heart-shaped glow or billowing cloud is not a figure. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
- unpainted_edge: true if any edge or corner fades into or shows bare white or cream paper, a blank band or an unpainted margin. Pale sky or cloud that continues the scene is not a margin.
- painted_frame: true if an ornamental border, gilt band or frame runs along the edges as part of the artwork. A window or doorway inside the scene is not a frame.
- lettering: true if letters, words, numerals, pseudo-script, inscriptions on objects such as tablets or scrolls, a signature or initials appear anywhere, including small marks in corners.
Each answer must agree with what you described. In reasons, name each fault you report and where it is; leave reasons empty when there are none.

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and put no text or writing in the scene. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

content.text:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Song of Solomon 2:1: "I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Shulammite

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Shulammite: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty; slender, graceful build; warm dark skin tanned by sun from working the vineyards; long dark hair, thick and flowing like goats descending Gilead, often partly veiled; large dove-like dark eyes, soft gaze, full lips, a fine chain at her neck; signature outfit a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep red woven wrap-cloak; signature prop a small wooden basket or a sprig of henna blossom.
- Only The Shulammite has this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: The Shulammite standing upright among blooming flowers, head slightly lifted
Action: She gestures gently toward the blossoms around her, presenting herself as the flower of the valley
Setting: Open valley of the Levant with spring flowers and scattered fields near a village
Secondary elements: Wild roses and lilies in the grass, distant vineyards and stone village houses, a shepherd's staff resting nearby
Mood: Tender, humble and quietly confident
Time of day: Late afternoon in spring, warm golden light with clear dry air and a light breeze
Composition: Medium shot from slightly below, subject at left third with the flowering valley opening to the right

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Isaiah son of Amoz

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.
- Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. Carries a glowing live coal held in long iron tongs, the coal burning orange-red.
- Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.
- Only Isaiah son of Amoz, Seraphim, Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Isaiah, a humble figure in plain linen, looking upward with head bowed slightly; above him the winged seraphim.
Action: Winged seraphim hover above the sanctuary, veiling their faces and feet with paired wings while two wings beat in flight.
Setting: Inside the temple in Jerusalem, a great hall of cedar and gold with tall pillars and a sanctuary altar.
Secondary elements: Lamps burning on stands, incense smoke drifting through the hall, and a glowing radiance of cloud and light filling the high sanctuary beyond the seraphim, with the hem of divine glory spilling across the floor.
Mood: Awe, reverence and holy stillness, with quiet human humility.
Time of day: Early morning in the temple; still air and soft golden lamplight.
Composition: Low viewpoint from the temple floor looking up at Isaiah in the foreground, with the seraphim arrayed above him and the luminous sanctuary filling the upper frame.

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Isaiah son of Amoz

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.
- Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. Carries a glowing live coal held in long iron tongs, the coal burning orange-red.
- Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.
- Only Isaiah son of Amoz, Seraphim, Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Isaiah, a humble figure in plain linen, looking upward with head bowed slightly; above him the winged seraphim.
Action: Winged seraphim hover above the sanctuary, veiling their faces and feet with paired wings while two wings beat in flight.
Setting: Inside the temple in Jerusalem, a great hall of cedar and gold with tall pillars and a sanctuary altar.
Secondary elements: Lamps burning on stands, incense smoke drifting through the hall, and a glowing radiance of cloud and light filling the high sanctuary beyond the seraphim, with the hem of divine glory spilling across the floor.
Mood: Awe, reverence and holy stillness, with quiet human humility.
Time of day: Early morning in the temple; still air and soft golden lamplight.
Composition: Low viewpoint from the temple floor looking up at Isaiah in the foreground, with the seraphim arrayed above him and the luminous sanctuary filling the upper frame.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

content.text:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, John 21:7: "That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Simon Peter; The beloved disciple; The Twelve Disciples (collective); Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.
- The beloved disciple: a young man of about thirty, lean and quick, with a sun-browned skin of the Galilean fishing shore. Dark brown hair cut just above the ears, a short, close beard, and a calm, steady, attentive face with deep-set eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark wool cloak of earth brown. He carries a simple wooden walking staff.
- Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. Low stone-built fishing villages and wooden fishing boats line the water, with nets drying on the shore. Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.
- The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Only Simon Peter, The beloved disciple, Sea of Galilee, The Twelve Disciples (collective), Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Simon Peter mid-leap, arms gathering his cloak, body angled forward toward the water
Action: Peter plunges from the boat into the shallows of the lake toward the shore.
Setting: Sea of Galilee near a stone-and-sand shore beside a fishing boat with a small charcoal fire.
Secondary elements: The beloved disciple points toward the shore from the boat; other disciples stand in the boat hauling a heavy net full of fish; a few oars and nets lie in the boat.
Mood: Eager urgency, joyful recognition and devotion.
Time of day: Early morning dawn, clear and calm with mist lifting off the water.
Composition: Low side view from the lake, Peter in the foreground splashing into the water, boat and disciples in the middle distance, shore and dim figure of Jesus beyond.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Simon Peter's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Simon Peter only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish.
- After: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.

6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.

Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):

- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Lazarus of Bethany, Crowd in John, Martha have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Action: Jesus calls out loudly while Lazarus, still wrapped in grave linens, stirs within the tomb mouth

Secondary elements: A gathered crowd of Judean onlookers in earth-toned tunics and cloaks watching in stunned silence, Martha close by with hands pressed to her chest, a stone rolled aside at the entrance
Mood: Awe, tense expectancy and reverent wonder
Time of day: Late afternoon, warm low sun shifting toward dusk in still, clear dry air with faint dust
Composition: Frontal view from within the crowd, tomb opening centered, Jesus and Lazarus framed by the dark entrance with the crowd spread across the foreground

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and put no text or writing in the scene. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.

content.text:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, John 11:43: "When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; Lazarus of Bethany; Crowd in John; Martha

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Lazarus of Bethany, Crowd in John, Martha have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Jesus standing at the tomb entrance, head lifted and arm extended in a commanding call
Action: Jesus calls out loudly while Lazarus, still wrapped in grave linens, stirs within the tomb mouth
Setting: Rock-cut tomb entrance near Bethany, pale limestone face on a hillside with olive trees
Secondary elements: A gathered crowd of Judean onlookers in earth-toned tunics and cloaks watching in stunned silence, Martha close by with hands pressed to her chest, a stone rolled aside at the entrance
Mood: Awe, tense expectancy and reverent wonder
Time of day: Late afternoon, warm low sun shifting toward dusk in still, clear dry air with faint dust
Composition: Frontal view from within the crowd, tomb opening centered, Jesus and Lazarus framed by the dark entrance with the crowd spread across the foreground

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
- After: He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and put no text or writing in the scene. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.
