PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Acts 9:3: "As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):

Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Saul of Tarsus (Paul); the men with Saul

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.
- The men with Saul: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, lean build from road travel; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beard; plain, weathered faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic with a brown wool travelling cloak in dusty earth tones. Carries a walking staff and a leather satchel.
- Damascus: a walled oasis city of pale limestone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs and domes, set against arid hills; date palms, orchards and irrigated gardens watered by the rivers Abanah and Pharpar; a city gate with a wall, and a straight main street lined with walls and shaded arcades.
- Only Saul of Tarsus (Paul), the men with Saul, Damascus have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Saul of Tarsus, a man in dusty traveling clothes, halted in the road with his head lifted toward the sky.
Action: A sudden blinding light pours down from the heavens and surrounds Saul as he stops.
Setting: Dusty desert road approaching Damascus, with distant walls and rooftops of a Roman-era city on the horizon.
Secondary elements: Companion travelers in plain tunics and cloaks stand back, shielding their eyes from the radiance; no figure is shown within the light itself.
Mood: Startled, awestruck and tense, with a sense of sudden holy disruption.
Time of day: Midday turning to late afternoon, clear dry hot sky with no rain, harsh sunlight overtaken by sudden radiance from above.
Composition: Wide view along the road with Saul centered mid-stride, the light radiating from above and the city walls small on the horizon.

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, John 11:43: "When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; Lazarus of Bethany; Crowd in John; Martha

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Lazarus of Bethany, Crowd in John, Martha have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Jesus standing at the tomb entrance, head lifted and arm extended in a commanding call
Action: Jesus calls out loudly while Lazarus, still wrapped in grave linens, stirs within the tomb mouth
Setting: Rock-cut tomb entrance near Bethany, pale limestone face on a hillside with olive trees
Secondary elements: A gathered crowd of Judean onlookers in earth-toned tunics and cloaks watching in stunned silence, Martha close by with hands pressed to her chest, a stone rolled aside at the entrance
Mood: Awe, tense expectancy and reverent wonder
Time of day: Late afternoon, warm low sun shifting toward dusk in still, clear dry air with faint dust
Composition: Frontal view from within the crowd, tomb opening centered, Jesus and Lazarus framed by the dark entrance with the crowd spread across the foreground

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
- After: He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.

1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Visionary heaven and renewal
People: Seers, heavenly beings and the redeemed as described.
Dress: Robes and garments with the text's colors and materials.
Buildings and objects: Thrones, altars, glass-like sea and jeweled city as described.
Technology: Ancient lamps, trumpets, harps, swords and sailing ships; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A renewed land and open sky, bright and still, with no sea.
Action: Radiant cloud and light spread across the new heaven, the first heaven and earth having passed away.
Setting: A newly made earth of green land and clear water-free expanse under a bright new sky.
Secondary elements: Radiant cloud and gentle light filling the sky; the place where the sea once was now dry, open land.
Mood: Awe, stillness and quiet hope at the dawn of renewal.
Time of day: Luminous, timeless daylight with no night; clear still air.
Composition: Wide view across the renewed land and sky, with radiant cloud filling the upper frame and the horizon open and unbroken.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Matthew 27:35: "When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Roman soldiers; Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.
- Golgotha: a rounded rocky knoll of pale limestone rising just outside the walls of Jerusalem, bare of trees and scrub except for thin dry grass in cracks. Its crown is worn smooth and bony-white, giving the hill its name, the place of a skull. A rough stone-cut quarry face and a few low olive trees stand at its foot, and the walls and towers of the city rise distant behind it.
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Only The Roman soldiers, Golgotha, Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Roman soldiers in bronze helmets and military tunics crouched or kneeling in a loose group, dividing cloth.
Action: Soldiers sort and portion out the garments, casting lots to decide who gets each piece.
Setting: Rocky summit of Golgotha outside Jerusalem's walls, with a stone road visible below.
Secondary elements: Folded cloaks and tunics spread on the ground; a tall wooden cross with the crucified figure seen at a distance, handled with restraint and no gore.
Mood: Sombre, detached and grave, with the quiet indifference of routine duty.
Time of day: Midday turning to afternoon; hot, still air with dust stirring and pale harsh daylight.
Composition: Mid-distance view from slightly below the hilltop, soldiers in the foreground framed against the sky, cross placed behind them.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- After: and they sat and watched him there.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Revelation 4:6: "Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Robes of deep crimson and white.
- Heavenly throne room: a vast open sanctuary of radiance beneath a heaven like crystal, floored with a sea of glass that is clear as crystal, set with a great throne and a temple whose doors open onto the heavens, lit by lightnings, thunders and a rainbow the colour of emerald about the throne. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.
- Only Four living creatures (Revelation), Heavenly throne room have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Four strange winged living creatures, their bodies covered with eyes, standing around and within the throne.
Action: They stand still in worship before the throne, their many eyes turned outward and forward.
Setting: A heavenly throne room with a glassy sea like crystal spread before the throne and a jeweled radiance around it.
Secondary elements: Faint wisps of cloud and rolling radiance drifting over the crystal sea, rays of light from the central throne reflected in its surface.
Mood: Awe, holiness and quiet reverence.
Time of day: Unchanging heavenly day with steady radiance and still, clear air.
Composition: A wide view from before the throne, with the sea of glass in the foreground and the creatures arranged around the central throne.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.

Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.
